parameters.content:
## Start
**GET /webhook/api/jobs** — the React app calls this to fill the job board. It answers once the list has been read.

## 1. Read the job list
One query returns **one row** holding the whole list as a JSON array (`jobs`). Aggregating in SQL means an empty table gives `[]` instead of no items, so the reply is always `{ "jobs": [] }` at worst.
Columns are renamed to the camelCase `JobSummary` shape the UI expects. Only the single owner's jobs; best match first, unscored jobs last, newest first on ties.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments. The parameters are
-- substituted everywhere in the text, comments included, which breaks the query.
select coalesce(
  json_agg(
    json_build_object(
      'id',               id,
      'title',            title,
      'employer',         employer,
      'advertiser',       advertiser,
      'shortDescription', short_description,
      'url',              url,
      'status',           status,
      'matchScore',       match_score,
      'warnings',         warnings,
      'extractionStatus', extraction_status,
      'sourceRemoved',    source_removed,
      'sourceRef',        source_ref,
      'createdAt',        to_char(created_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')
    )
    order by match_score desc nulls last, created_at desc
  ),
  '[]'::json
) as jobs
from jobs
where owner_id = $1;
